title: Media queries and breakpoints
learningObjectives: Explain media queries and breakpoints and apply responsive design principles.

understand.concept: Media queries apply CSS conditionally based on media features such as viewport width, orientation, colour scheme, and reduced-motion preference. Breakpoints should be chosen where the content or layout needs to change, not only for specific device names.
understand.whyItMatters: Content-led breakpoints are more resilient as devices and browser windows vary. Prefer a small number of meaningful changes and test just above and below each threshold.
understand.analogy: A breakpoint is a point where a layout changes its arrangement because the available space no longer suits the current arrangement.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; responsive behaviour is determined by CSS layout and viewport/container conditions.

explain.narrative: The cards stack on narrow screens and form three columns when the viewport reaches the chosen content-led breakpoint.

examples.explanation: The cards stack on narrow screens and form three columns when the viewport reaches the chosen content-led breakpoint.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the responsive behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Resize the preview around 42rem. Choose a different breakpoint based on when your card text becomes cramped.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive page section and test it at narrow, medium, and wide viewport sizes, including longer labels.
hints: Use the browser responsive viewport tools.
Check horizontal overflow and text scaling.
Keep keyboard access and semantic structure intact.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice of a responsive breakpoint?
options: Where the content or layout needs to change
questions.answer: Where the content or layout needs to change
questions.explanation: Breakpoints should respond to the needs of the content rather than device labels.

questions.prompt: What should be included in responsive testing?
options: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.answer: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.explanation: Responsive defects often appear at intermediate widths or with expanded content.
